image_description: A close-up, front-facing view of a single circular loudspeaker driver (woofer) with a grey metallic frame and a dark grey cone. The speaker features a central dust cap, a visible rubber or foam surround, and mounting holes around the perimeter of the frame. The background is plain white.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The cone surface has an overly smooth, airbrushed gradient appearance lacking the fine micro-texture typical of paper or polypropylene cones. It looks slightly synthetic.
The mounting holes around the perimeter are irregular in shape and spacing. Some appear partially melted or non-circular, suggesting geometric instability in the generation process.
The outer metallic rim shows slight waviness and inconsistent thickness, deviating from the perfect circular rigidity expected of a manufactured metal part.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of audio component and rule out misclassification as other circular mechanical parts.
To verify the structural integrity of the mounting holes and the boundary between the cone and the surround.
To assess the realism of the materials and detect subtle rendering artifacts like the smoothness of the cone.

focus_areas: Texture realism of the speaker cone
Boundary sharpness between cone and surround
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the mounting holes; AI often struggles with repeating geometric patterns like screw holes, leading to melting or irregular shapes. Also, evaluate if the 'smoothness' of the cone is a stylistic choice or a lack of high-frequency texture detail typical of AI generation.
